text: {"standards":[{"code":"RL.6.2","verdict":"partly","reason":"Part B's quick write asks students to write a 3–4 sentence summary naming a theme word and one cited detail, which touches the theme and summary skill, but the theme is named with a single model sentence and does not require determining how the theme is conveyed through a range of particular details or an objective summary of the full text."},{"code":"RL.6.3","verdict":"partly","reason":"Part A's two-column before/after chart and Pulse Check ask students to note how Percy and Annabeth change, but the lesson never has students map the plot as a series of episodes leading toward resolution, so the plot-unfolding part of the standard is not taught."},{"code":"L.6.6","verdict":"taught","reason":"The Vocabulary in Context activity and the Part B quick write have students define and use the Outline's words such as trust, sacrifice and betrayal in their own sentences and summaries, which meets the acquire-and-use goal for academic words."}],"anchorText":{"verdict":"partly","reason":"The lesson names pp. 320–326 of The Lightning Thief and has students reread them in Part A, but the Outline's film-comparison component is included, and the Lesson's text-and-film contrast relies on an unspecified film scene rather than the named pages, so the text use is only partly tied to the Outline's named material."}}
